name: NTN-HO Benchmark
description: "NTN-HO Benchmark is a simulation-derived, closed-loop benchmark for evaluating handover policies in direct-to-cell non-terrestrial networks with terrestrial and low-Earth-orbit access. The benchmark contains 276 scenario-disjoint one-hour scenarios and 3,038 data files in Apache Parquet, JSON, and TLE formats. Physical and link-layer states are generated at 1-second resolution, while handover decisions are evaluated every 5 seconds. Each decision provides the serving action and up to 12 candidate handover actions. Action-specific counterfactual outcomes are recorded at 10-, 30-, 60-, and 120-second horizons, including radio-link-failure risk, interruption, access success, execution delay, delivered traffic, and recovery outcomes. Official Train, Calibration, Validation, Test, Confirmation, and out-of-distribution partitions support fitting, calibration, model selection, and held-out evaluation without scenario leakage. Current and historical policy observations are stored separately from future-derived labels to prevent inference leakage. The benchmark is simulation-derived and contains no human-participant, clinical, or personally identifiable data. It is intended for reproducible research and should not be interpreted as field-validated deployment performance."
